record.paper_title: Solutions to four open problems on quorum colorings of graphs
record.context_brief: Relation between ψ_q(G) and defensive alliance number
record.original_question: Is the condition ψ_q(G) = 1 equivalent to the conjunction that the defensive alliance number a(G) equals ⌈n/2⌉ and the order n = |V(G)| is odd? Here a defensive alliance is a subset S of V(G) such that every v in S has at least as many vertices of N[v] inside S as outside S.

evidence.quote: Is ψq(G) = 1 if and only if a(G) =⌈n/2⌉ and n is odd?
which therefore answers also Question 2 in negative.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph of order $n=|V(G)|$. For a vertex $v\in V$, let $N[v]$ denote the closed neighborhood of $v$. A subset $S\subseteq V$ is called a defensive alliance if for every $v\in S$, $|N[v]\cap S|\ge |N[v]\setminus S|$. The defensive alliance number $a(G)$ is the minimum cardinality of a defensive alliance of $G$.

A quorum coloring of $G$ is a partition of $V$ into color classes $V_1,\dots,V_k$ such that for every vertex $v\in V$, at least half of the vertices of $N[v]$ lie in the same color class as $v$ (equivalently, each color class is a defensive alliance). Let $\psi_q(G)$ denote the maximum number of color classes in a quorum coloring of $G$.

Decide whether the following equivalence holds for every graph $G$:
$$\psi_q(G)=1 \iff a(G)=\left\lceil \tfrac{n}{2}\right\rceil \text{ and } n \text{ is odd}.$$
Either prove the equivalence or exhibit a counterexample.
artifact.status_search_result: The equivalence has been resolved in the negative. A 2021 paper in RAIRO – Operations Research, "Solutions to four open problems on quorum colorings of graphs," answers this question negatively, also showing that there is no good characterization of graphs with ψ_q(G)=1 unless P = NP ∩ co-NP.
